input: A measured-label existence check for 13 typed Rubin cohort objects uses a public spectrum archive whose live site returns HTTP 403 on every path. Its Internet Archive object pages return 404 for all 13 cohort objects and also for 10 non-cohort control objects that were classified in 2026. The report proposes to record that none of the 13 cohort objects has a public classification spectrum, so the cohort's measured label count is 0. Rule.

A monthly label-pricing table states that 485 labelled Rubin cohort objects will be reached by March 2027. It takes the Rubin return to sky as 2026-11-01 because 'the storm repairs typically take about three months', although no primary source gives a return date, and it uses 30 usable P60 nights per month with no source. Rule.

The same table is instead built from a calendar model frozen and hashed before computing: P60-class usable nights per month from a declared query of the same-site ZTF P48 science-exposure archive (2021-2024, usable = at least half the month's 90th-percentile nightly exposure count), Rubin on-sky fraction 10 of 15 nights from the scheduler record, capacity and purity grids with seed locators, and months reported as a function of every candidate return month from 2026-10 to 2027-09 with the calendar completion date left UNDEMONSTRATED. Months implied by existing 2026 name-server throughput are labelled upper bounds because the throughput counts are lower bounds. A reviewer proposes to refuse the table because the Rubin return date is unknown. Dispose.

The table's spectra count for 485 labels at purity 0.93, classification success 0.93 and 8 spectra per night is 561 in both the wave-3 table and the wave-4 monthly table; the wave-4 script asserts equality for every row at zero existing labels and adds a separate sensitivity row using 13 existence-only cohort labels. A verifier notes the two waves' files differ in size and columns and proposes to block the wave-4 table as an unexplained change to a ruling-bearing number. Dispose.
